title: A nonzero polynomial has positive root multiplicity at c exactly when it vanishes at c
statement: Let $K$ be a field, $T$ an indeterminate, $K[T]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-polynomial-ring], $c\in K$, and for $P\in K[T]$ let $m_c(P)$ be the multiplicity of $c$ as a root of $P$ [def-weil-root-multiplicity] and $P(c)\in K$ the value of $P$ at $c$ [def-weil-polynomial-root]. For nonzero $P\in K[T]$: $m_c(P)\geq1$ if and only if $P(c)=0$; equivalently $m_c(P)=0$ if and only if $P(c)\neq0$.

source.place: ## Proof, third and fourth paragraphs: the factors $P_i$ with $P_i(c)\neq0$ are treated as contributing nothing to the pole at $T=c$; the equivalence is used without proof (it is also recorded in the statement of def-weil-root-multiplicity, 'by the factor theorem')
